subject: psychology

moments.title: Illumination experiments begin
moments.body: Studies of lighting and productivity produce confusing results: productivity rises whether illumination is increased or decreased.
moments.takeaway: Confounds in field studies can yield more interesting findings than intended.

moments.title: Studies conclude
moments.body: The relay assembly studies become the basis for human relations management theory.
moments.takeaway: Industrial studies could reshape management as much as psychology.

moments.title: Re-analysis
moments.body: Re-analysis of the original Hawthorne data suggests effects were smaller and more time-dependent than the textbook account claims.
moments.takeaway: Foundational findings can shrink under scrutiny.

now.title: Observer effects in research
now.body: Modern research-design teaching cites Hawthorne effects in trials, ethnography and program evaluation.
now.open_questions: How should studies be designed to minimise or estimate observer effects?

reflection: The 'Hawthorne effect' is more rhetorical device than well-measured phenomenon.
